notes: §1985:XI.4.3.3 SR1: "The storage area associated with identifier-1 and the record area associated with file-name-1 must not be the same storage area." RETURN INTO reaches CheckIntoReceiver, whose CheckPhraseOperandIsNotRecordArea refuses (COBOL6827, below 2023 via RecordAreaRule.InForce) when StorageSharing.IsRecordAreaOf holds: any 01 of the SD, or a subordinate at offset 0 of the record's full width. Probes at --std 85: INTO the 01 (witness), a second 01 of the SD, the full-width only child SRT-KEY, and an 01 holding an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table are refused; INTO a WS item runs (GOT AAAAA / GOT BBBBB); a shorter tail item is accepted (not the same area); --std 2023 accepts. Gap: IsRecordAreaOf answers false for EVERY reference-modified operand and every item under an OCCURS, so a literal reference modification covering the whole record, RETURN SRT-FILE INTO SRT-REC (1:5) over a 5-character record, and INTO E (1) where 01 SRT-REC3. 05 E OCCURS 1 PIC X(5), both the identical storage area, compile and run. kb/Work PB5412 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-03.json). || RE-VERDICTED CONFORMS (kb/Work PB5412, wave 20262025 group B): StorageSharing.IsRecordAreaOf decides 'the same storage area' on the storage the operand denotes (StorageExtent.OfReference), not on its form, so a literal reference modification of the whole record (R (1:10); R (1:) whatever R's length), the element of a table of one occurrence and a 66 THROUGH alias of the whole record are refused COBOL6827, and a SAME AREA peer's record is the area too (1985:VII.2.13.4 GR1, FileModel.StorageSharingFiles); docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(b) is revised. The read-3 and read-4 probes are all refused now.

next.reason: 1985: "The storage area associated with identifier-1 and the record area associated with file-name-1 must not be the same storage area."; 2023: "14.6.10, Overlapping operands, and 14.9.25 ... apply to any cases in which the storage area identified by identifier-1 and the record area". 1985 syntax rule forbids identifier-1 being the record area. 2023 drops the prohibition and applies the overlapping-operand MOVE rules, leaving the result undefined only if the MOVE is undefined.
